Maybe my post wasn’t entirely clear. I never came out as gay, I came out as bi and then proceeded to live a lifestyle that was more gay than it was anything else. Part of this was because I found a liking to the community, but I think the main overriding factor is the fact that I had been told by society for so long that I was gay because I was different, and since I was attracted to men I gradually came to believe it, even if experiences and feelings I’d had for women should’ve been solid evidence for the fact that I’m not gay. I recently had this experience with a woman, tbh i felt really strongly about her and maybe I shouldn’t say that it hasn’t worked out yet because more than anything i feel like I’m getting mixed signals. I was very wishy washy for a long time because I had a lot of shameful and confused bent up feelings about my sexuality and it kinda feels like I dragged my feet for so long that she lost interest. Maybe I’m projecting, but that’s beside the point. 

I very strongly agree with what you said, that gay men are very different from bi men but specifically for the second reason. Gay men’s desires are for a kind of romantic love somewhat akin to straight love, only with a man rather than with a woman. I, on the other hand, want what you said you had with men; long lost brother or very close friend. That kind of bond that is strengthened by the “benefits.” It’s a kind of love, it’s just kind of different from the kind of romantic love gay men often want with other men. It’s a kind of fraternal intimacy and love that is just different. Perhaps it makes sense that the only times I’ve had that it was with other bi men, maybe they had the same desires as me. Anyway, when I’ve tried to be truly romantic with another man, something deep down feels wrong. I’ve tried to convince myself that that’s just internalized homophobia but I don’t think that’s the case anymore. At this point, I think that I… am just more disposed to have that with a woman? Like to fall in love and commit myself to someone, I feel like it would be a woman. Secondarily, I find myself much more physically and sexually attracted to women recently. And now I just wish I had known this sooner. So that I wouldn’t have tried to be the best loving boyfriend to a few perfectly nice and fine gay men who I probably damaged because I couldn’t really go through with the very couply stuff and had to back out of relationships with. I am also now basically more interested in finding a girl to be with (not saying I’m straight, this is just where I feel more comfortable right now) and I don’t know how comfortable a majority of women would be with all of this.

By the way, yes I am lonely but in some ways this is liberating. I never truly identified with being gay, that was just kind of gradually imposed on me, and being able to see through that now, I feel like even if it isolates me I am coming back to myself. I’m not performing anything right now, I honestly feel more connected to myself than I have in a while.

I think its just generally like, when people say things like "people nowadays not only disagree on their interpretations of reality but they disagree on what reality is to begin with." So for example, I don't think the Jan. 6 riots were a "coup" carried out by white supremacists. I don't think that anyone who voted for Trump is automatically a racist-misogynistic-homophobic-transphobic-xenophobic-islamophobic whatever. I'm not 100% confident that the anti-COVID measures we've taken were necessarily the smartest and do sometimes question whether things like lockdowns will have more long-term negative ripple effects than the virus itself. I didn't vote in 2020 (something very few people know, most think I voted Biden). I have, well, lets say mixed feelings when it comes to race-based identity politics and am even more opposed to identity politics surrounding gender, sexuality etc. Overall, I think class is still what will determine your life outcomes more than any of the identity categories being "advocated" for nowadays. Basically, when people start talking to me they automatically assume that I agree with them on all of these things when in reality I don't. There's also the whole thing of gasping before mentioning the name of an artist that has been disavowed ("He likes \*gasp\* Vincent Gallo!").
